abort.already_configured: The integration already has an entry for this group of this provider, or for this address.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The entry now uses the new group or the new address. To update the entity IDs, open the device and select Recreate entity IDs.
abort.reconfigure_unchanged: The entry already uses this group and this address. Nothing changed.
abort.provider_removed: Version 0.11.0 of the integration removed the source {provider}, so Reconfigure cannot change this entry. The source stopped giving the outage schedule to other programs. The integration has no other source of this schedule. Delete this entry: go to Settings > Devices & services > {integration}, open the menu of this entry, and select Delete.
abort.yasno_connection_error:
Failed to get the Yasno groups.
The Yasno API is unreachable, or it has no groups for this provider now.
Make sure that Home Assistant can connect to the Internet, and try again later.
{url}
abort.dtek_json_unavailable:
No data source gave a schedule that the integration can read.
The source is unreachable, or its data has a format that the integration does not know.
Make sure that Home Assistant can connect to the Internet, and try again later.
{urls}
abort.dtek_json_empty_data:
The data source answered, but its schedule has no groups now.
This can happen when the provider publishes no outages.
Try again later.
{urls}

group_not_listed.title: No outage schedule for group {group}
group_not_listed.description:
The source {provider} has no outage schedule for group {group}. Until the source has it, the Electricity sensor shows Unknown, and the calendars show no outages for this group.

The provider can renumber or remove groups. Find your group on the website of the provider. To change the group, go to Settings > Devices & services > {integration}, open the menu of this entry, and select Reconfigure.

This message disappears when the source has group {group} again.

address_not_found.title: Yasno does not find the address of {entry}
address_not_found.description:
Yasno does not know the address of the entry «{entry}» any more. The integration keeps the schedule of the group {group}. Look for the address on the Yasno site: {url}. To give the entry the address as Yasno writes it now, go to Settings > Devices & services > {integration}, open the menu of this entry, select Reconfigure, and then select By address.

This message disappears when Yasno finds the address again.

provider_removed.title: Version 0.11.0 removed the source of {entry}
provider_removed.description:
Version 0.11.0 of the integration removed the source {provider}, so the integration cannot load the entry «{entry}». The source stopped giving the outage schedule to other programs. The integration has no other source of this schedule. To delete the entry, go to Settings > Devices & services > {integration}, open the menu of this entry, and select Delete.

This message disappears when you delete the entry.

refresh_failed.message: Failed to get a new outage schedule, because the source did not answer. The entities keep the last schedule. Make sure that Home Assistant can connect to the Internet, and try again later.

check_group_failed.message: Yasno gave no sure answer about the address, so the group stays. Try again in a few minutes.

check_group_not_listed.message: Yasno gives the group {group} for the address, but its schedule does not list that group yet. The entry keeps its group.

address_not_found.message: Yasno does not find the address of this entry. The entry keeps its group.
